newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia bonds flop after early U.S. flip.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia bonds flop after early U.S. flip.

text.p: *Australian bond futures ended with pared gains as the market failed to capitalise on an early U.S.-led rally to two months highs in fairly slow activity.
*U.S. holiday, caution ahead of RBA Bulletin limit trade.
Australian bond futures pared their initial U.S. inspired advance as the market found few takers as the 10-year bond contract struck a two-month high.
A U.S. holiday for Presidents Day and caution ahead of Tuesday's Reserve Bank quarterly Bulletin kept trading interest to a minimum, as did the absence of any key local data.

A break of resistance of 92.720 in SYCOM trading on March 10-year bond futures contract failed to draw in computerised technical accounts, and saw the market make a gradual slip back and through this level going into the close.

The RBA Bulletin will be the key focus on Tuesday, although the market already has some insight into what it may bring following a brief assessment on the economy by the central bank governor Ian Macfarlane last week.
Analysts expect the report to show the economy doing reasonably well and that inflation remains subdued.

"But wages of course are the wild card at the moment and we need to see how low wages are going, or if they are in fact falling any further, before we expect to see any move in interest rates," said Stephen Koukoulas, chief economist at Citibank Australia.

However, Citibank give very little chance to there being a further reduction in official interest rates, and a Reuters survey of economists taken on Friday found only a 30 percent chance of such a move.
The RBA has already expressed caution on wages and in particular it wants to see the outcome to the trade union's 8.75 percent "living wage" claim, which is due in early March.
Meanwhile, U.S. Treasuries firmed on Friday following a 0.3 percent rise in the headline PPI for January, the first drop since October 1994. There was no trading in U.S. during Tokyo trading.

The afternoon pull-back saw the Australian/U.S. 10-year yield slither through support at 100 basis points having narrowed in early trading. The local market continues to underperform Canadian debt, which remains upbeat ahead of Tuesday's federal budget.
